title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 3
statement: Suppose \(x\) and \(y\) are real numbers such that \(-1<x<y<1\). Let \(G\) be the sum of the geometric series whose first term is \(x\) and whose ratio is \(y\), and let \(G^{\prime}\) be the sum of the geometric series whose first term is \(y\) and ratio is \(x\). If \(G=G^{\prime}\), find \(x+y\).

solutions.text: 1 We note that \(G=x /(1-y)\) and \(G^{\prime}=y /(1-x)\). Setting them equal gives \(x /(1-y)=\) \(y /(1-x) \Rightarrow x^{2}-x=y^{2}-x \Rightarrow(x+y-1)(x-y)=0\), so we get that \(x+y-1=0 \Rightarrow x+y=1\).
